comment: Table 2.2 marks the shared library of agreed data structures (the Logical Information Model Repository) as optional at the start, and the component write-up calls it a progressive enabler rather than a prerequisite. But Section 3.6.2 says this same library is what systems are checked against to confirm they are built correctly. If a country skips it early, there is nothing to check against, so the idea of confirming that systems "follow the standard" has no basis yet.

public.suggestedRevision: Say what minimum data-structure control a country still needs early on, for example a small set of nationally agreed templates (profiles) to test against, so that checking whether systems follow the standard is not pushed entirely to a later stage.
